title: I am he (John 18:1–11)
hook: the soldiers fall back at his words

segments.voice: Yesterday, ecumenism, and the prayer that closed the supper: that they all may be one.

A garden at night, across a small valley from the city walls. Olive trees, the smell of crushed leaves, and down the slope a line of lights coming up: torches and lanterns, a detachment of soldiers, officers from the chief priests, the glint of weapons. Leading them is someone who knows exactly where to find this garden, because Jesus often met his disciples here. It's Judas. A chase in the dark would be the obvious next scene. John tells it very differently.
screen: `A GARDEN ACROSS THE KIDRON.` → `TORCHES COMING UP THE SLOPE.` → `JUDAS KNOWS THE PLACE.`

segments.voice: John says Jesus knew all that was coming upon him, and he went forth. He doesn't wait to be found. He walks out to meet them and asks, whom seek ye? Jesus of Nazareth, they say. And he answers with two words, in Greek egō eimi, which the Douay-Rheims renders: "I am he." Then John adds this: "As soon therefore as he had said to them: I am he; they went backward, and fell to the ground." Armed men, with torches, fall over. John doesn't explain it. But the reader has been hearing egō eimi all through this Gospel: I am the bread of life, I am the light of the world, and once, startlingly, before Abraham was made, I am. In the scriptures, I am is how God names himself to Moses at the burning bush. So when Jesus says it in the garden, John lets the words land with weight, and the arresting party ends up on the ground. He asks again, whom seek ye, and gets the same answer. Then: if you seek me, let these go their way. He trades himself for his friends, the good shepherd in a single sentence. Peter draws a sword and cuts off the right ear of the high priest's servant, and John gives us the servant's name: Malchus. Jesus stops him: put up thy sword into the scabbard. He isn't trapped here. He's choosing. And it all begins with saying, plainly, who he is.
screen: `HE GOES OUT TO MEET THEM.` · `EGŌ EIMI: I AM HE.` · `THEY FALL TO THE GROUND.` · `LET THESE GO THEIR WAY.` · then, large: `I AM HE.`

segments.voice: If you can, stand, feet flat and shoulders easy, and say your own name once, quietly, not as a question. Then picture one place where you tend to hide who you are, or what you believe, or what you did, and see yourself there simply answering, that's me. If you pray, hold Jesus's words, I am he, and ask for courage; if you don't, just stand and breathe.
Egō eimi. Jesus's answer to the soldiers in the garden, I am he, and they fall back to the ground. Today's word.
Your line: put up thy sword. He met the torches with two words. Day five hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: The arrest in the garden opens the Passion according to John, which Catholics hear on Good Friday; on Holy Thursday night, some parishes keep a watch of prayer after the evening Mass, remembering the garden.
